clauses.reason: Section 1 (designation of officers of the Department of Agriculture to act as Secretary when the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are unavailable) had no own-terms end. It remained operative until EO 13241 of December 18, 2001, whose Sec. 4 states "Executive Order 11957 of January 13, 1977, is hereby revoked." (66 FR 66258). EO 13241 has no delayed effective date, and its Sec. 1 to 3 replace the succession with a new order of succession in Agriculture, so the revocation is the first end of this command.

Section 2 states "Executive Order No. 11793 of July 10, 1974, is hereby revoked." This is a one-time, self-executing revocation of another order; it was performed when EO 11957 was signed on January 13, 1977 (the order has no delayed effective date), so its first end is the signing date by performance, not the later revocation of EO 11957 in 2001. The ending source is the held original text of the order, which contains the quoted sentence.

conflict_resolutions.WHOLE_END_ACTOR_DISAGREEMENT: The catalog disagreement names EO 13240 and EO 13241 as whole-order revokers. The held text of EO 13240 (Council of Europe GRECO designation, 66 FR 66257) does not mention Executive Order 11957 at all, so the catalog note attached to EO 13240 that says it revokes EO 11957 is not supported by its text; the held text of EO 13241 (66 FR 66258) states in Sec. 4: "Executive Order 11957 of January 13, 1977, is hereby revoked." The whole-order end therefore rests on EO 13241 alone.

research_rationale:
EO 11957 (January 13, 1977) designated officers of the Department of Agriculture to act as Secretary of Agriculture (Sec. 1) and revoked EO 11793 (Sec. 2). It has no own-terms sunset. Its Sec. 1 designation stayed operative until EO 13241 of December 18, 2001 revoked the whole order in its Sec. 4; Sec. 2 was a self-executing revocation of EO 11793 performed on signing. The status is NO: EO 13241 Sec. 4 ended the order, and the three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) found no later instrument reviving it.

savings.reason: EO 13241 contains no savings clause preserving EO 11957: its Sec. 3 only reserves presidential discretion over designation of an acting Secretary, and its Sec. 4 revokes EO 11957 without exception. The earlier revocation of EO 11793 in Sec. 2 of EO 11957 was complete on signing and is not revived by the revocation of EO 11957. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, eCFR and the OFR catalog found no continuing reliance on EO 11957.
